prompt:
A hand-painted map of a whole continent seen from directly above, in the manner of a painted fantasy map such as a map of Middle-earth: coastlines, mountain ranges drawn as shaded ridges, rivers as fine dark lines running downhill to the sea, forests as textured masses, marsh, desert and open plain each in its own tone. Oil on parchment in a 19th-century academic manner with a smooth, finely blended surface, soft glazed transitions, fine detail, no heavy impasto. Palette of umber, ochre, gold, olive and sea-green with near-black shading. Less detail at larger scale; nothing drawn smaller than a hill or a wood; no settlements, no roads, no figures, no borders between countries. No text, no lettering, no compass rose, no scale bar, no frame, no grid, not photographic. The whole sheet is land and sea; nothing is cut off at the edges.

One large continent fills most of a square sheet, north at the top, with sea along every margin: a narrow strip of sea along the west edge, a narrow cold sea along the north edge, and a broader sea-green sea along the south and south-east, about a sixth of the sheet. A long folded mountain range runs north to south down the western third of the land, highest and widest in its middle with snow on its peaks, dark fir forest on its eastern slopes, and a narrow cliff coast on its far western side. At its northern end the range drops into steep wooded hills; a river gathers from the north-western uplands, crosses a patch of low marsh, and runs north through a clear gap in those hills across a small lowland to the northern sea. Between the range and the middle of the land, in the north-west, lies upland hill country cut into several closed river valleys, each separated by ridges, their rivers running east and north-east. In the exact center of the continent lies a wide, shallow, pale, bare basin of ashen ochre, about a tenth of the sheet across, ringed by worn low brown hills, with no river leaving it and a single small dark rounded mound at its middle. The whole north-east and east of the land is a wide open grass steppe in pale gold: along its northern edge, broken stony hills fall to the north-east coast, crossed by two rivers running north to the sea; on its eastern side the grass breaks into long parallel ridges like waves. In the south-center, a long river rises in the hills just east of the central basin and runs south-west and then south across wide olive-green farmed lowlands to a great dark-green delta marsh on the southern coast. The south-east coast is low and drowned: many small islands, creeks and pale tidal flats, and the broad estuary of a second big river that comes down from the southern edge of the steppe, with a pale shallow shelf of lighter sea-green water offshore. In the south-west, below the southern end of the range, low wooded hills in olive and umber are crossed by a slow river that makes one great bend before reaching the south-western sea. No desert, no ice sheet, no jungle.
